root_idea.summary: The root centers on heaviness as the opposite of lightness, extending to physical weight, burden, preponderance, gravity, and significance.
root_idea.development: Its basic physical sense develops into abstract heaviness and preponderance, burdens carried by people or the earth, moral burdens, and figurative gravity; derived forms express making heavy, being burdened, or hanging back under a weight.

qac_form_accounting.reason: This feminine singular passive-participial form is presented under the normalized masculine singular citation form.
This masculine plural passive-participial form is an inflection of the same lexical item as مُثْقَلَة.
The QAC group combines the plural أَثْقَال and the distinct dual expression الثَّقَلَانِ; both are retained under an explicitly composite public headword.

senses.definition: To become heavy or weighty; to be preponderant.
senses.usage_conditions: In the weighing of deeds, it describes the good deeds becoming preponderant in the scales.

senses.definition: To be momentous, formidable, or difficult to apprehend.
senses.usage_conditions: Used of the Hour in the expression ثَقُلَتْ فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالأَرْضِ; the usage conveys its gravity or formidable character, with an associated interpretation of its being difficult to know or apprehend.

senses.definition: To become heavy with pregnancy; to become gravid.
senses.usage_conditions: Used of a pregnant female when the pregnancy becomes apparent or the burden in the womb becomes heavy.

senses.definition: To hang back heavily, become sluggish, or incline under a weight.
senses.usage_conditions: In the Quranic construction with إِلَى, it describes holding back from action and inclining toward the earth or the present worldly life.

senses.definition: A weight or a quantity equal in weight; a measure used to express even a very small amount.
senses.usage_conditions: Used in constructions measuring something by its equivalent weight, including the weight of a tiny particle or mustard seed.
Used of one who bears a load or burden; the Quranic forms include a feminine singular and a masculine plural.
Primarily physical or relative to another thing; it may also be substantivized in a phrase contrasting light and heavy loads or conditions.
Used of an abstract matter or saying, especially a saying or matter whose seriousness or gravity is emphasized.

senses.definition: In a light-and-heavy pair: in difficult, weighty, or less readily undertaken circumstances.
senses.usage_conditions: In خِفَافًا وَثِقَالًا, it covers going forth whether readily or with difficulty and, by contextual interpretation, differing states such as being heavily equipped, ill, weak, old, or otherwise less ready; these are contextual applications of the contrast, not separate lexical meanings.

senses.definition: A load, burden, or weight carried.
senses.usage_conditions: The plural أَثْقَال refers to loads or burdens borne in travel and similar contexts.

senses.definition: The burdens brought out by the earth, including buried treasures or the dead bodies it contains.
senses.usage_conditions: Used in أَثْقَالُ الأَرْضِ, whose Quranic interpretation includes the earth's buried treasures and the bodies committed to it.

senses.definition: Sins or moral burdens, including the sins of those led astray by another.
senses.usage_conditions: Used of the burdens borne on account of one's own wrongdoing and, in the cited construction, additional burdens connected with misleading others.

senses.definition: The two weighty classes: humankind and the jinn.
senses.usage_conditions: The dual expression الثَّقَلَانِ is used for these two classes of rational creatures.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To be burdensome, onerous, oppressive, afflictive, or difficult for someone; of food, to be difficult to digest.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Often construed with عَلَى when something weighs heavily on a person.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To be or make a word or sound heavy and not easy to utter or hear.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A conventional linguistic and phonetic use, opposed to making pronunciation light or easy.

other_classical_meanings.definition: For hearing to become dull or partially impaired.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The expression فِي أُذُنِهِ ثِقَلٌ describes heaviness or dullness in the ear.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become heavy or debilitated through sickness or disease.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The usage describes the bodily effect of illness, including becoming heavy in sleep.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become slow, sluggish, indolent, dull, torpid, or lacking alacrity.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: May describe reluctance or slowness in receiving what is said or required.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of the shoots of certain plants, to become luxuriant, succulent, or sappy.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Attested of the shoots of العرفج and الثمام.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To test the weight of something by lifting it.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The object is lifted by hand to determine whether it is heavy or light.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To surpass or outweigh another thing in weight.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used in comparison of two things in weighing.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To make someone or something heavy, whether physically or figuratively.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The causative is the opposite of making light and includes imposing heaviness or weight.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To burden someone heavily or beyond their power; to overwhelm them with a burden.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The burden may be a load, debt, sickness, sleep, or meanness, which overcomes and weighs down the person.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To press heavily or bear one's weight upon a thing.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The construction may describe physical pressure or the act of putting one's weight on something.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To deem someone or something heavy, burdensome, or unwelcome.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The form is the converse of deeming something light or easy.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To be overcome and rendered heavy by sleep, sickness, or meanness.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is a passive or resultative use of the judgment that something has become heavy.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A traveller's belongings, household goods, baggage, apparatus, and accompanying household or retinue.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The term can denote the collection of things and people accompanying a person on a journey.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The requisites, apparatus, instruments, or tools belonging to a person or craft.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Examples include a learned person's books and writing reeds and a craftsman's equipment.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Something held in high estimation, much requested, and preserved with care.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The meaning is conventional in the expression for two valued objects or trusts.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The eggs of an ostrich.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized lexical usage explained by the pleasure and food they provide to whoever takes them.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Heaviness, weightiness, ponderousness, gravity, or preponderance.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The noun is primarily used of corporeal objects and then extended to ideal or abstract objects.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A fit of drowsiness or a heaviness and languor in the body.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: It may describe heaviness in the chest or body after food and heaviness experienced at the heart.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a woman, heavy or large in the hinder part; also heavy in an abstract sense.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The bodily description is a specialized lexical usage; the abstract extension is also attested.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a person, heavy through illness, or socially dull, sluggish, or unwelcome to companions; sometimes, in praise, grave and sedate.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The negative social sense is common, while the positive sense describes a grave, steady, or composed person.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a horse or camel, slow.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is an application to an animal's pace rather than to its physical mass alone.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become heavy through sickness or disease.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The active participial form ثَاقِلٌ can describe one who has become heavy because of illness.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A full-weight, non-deficient dinar.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A technical monetary description; its plural is ثَوَاقِلُ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Weighed down or oppressed by sickness or debt.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is a specialization of being burdened, attested independently for illness and financial obligation.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a woman, gravid, with the burden of pregnancy heavy or manifest.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The active participle describes the woman as carrying the pregnancy rather than the pregnancy's causative effect.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Ill received, disapproved, or not made an object of love to hearts.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative passive use describing social or emotional rejection.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A marble stone or piece of marble used to weigh down a carpet.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized object name derived from the function of making something heavy.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An object used for weighing, such as one of the weights of a balance.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This denotes the physical weighing implement rather than an amount measured by it.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A standardized unit of weight.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Classical accounts give variant specifications for the unit, including a known fraction or multiple of a dirham.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A gold coin or dinar.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A monetary use distinct from the general meaning of an amount equal in weight.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A person's weight or burden imposed upon another.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: In the idiom أَلْقَى عَلَيْهِ مَثَاقِيلَهُ, it refers to the burden or support that one person places upon another.

other_classical_meanings.definition: One who bears his weight upon a thing or presses heavily.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The derived participle can describe the manner of treading or applying pressure.

cautions: The QAC group v~aqalaAn combines the plural أَثْقَال with the distinct dual expression الثَّقَلَانِ; the public headword and usage conditions make both lexical identities explicit.
The alternatives attached to ثِقَالًا in the light-and-heavy construction are contextual interpretations of one contrast, not separate senses.
Some Lane Quran references use historical citation notation; the modern verse locations used here come only from the supplied QAC occurrence data.
